body:
> PhysicalBone3D can't be detected by Area3D

I'm not very familiar with the skeleton side of things, but it would seem that the problem here might be a misunderstanding of the `Skeleton3D.get_bone_global_pose` method.

Your code in `player_model.gd`:

```gd
if not physical_bone_simulator_3d.is_simulating_physics():
    bone.global_transform = skeleton_3d.get_bone_global_pose(0)
```

... ends up setting the bone's global position to `(0, 0, 0)` every time.

If you look at [the documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_skeleton3d.html#class-skeleton3d-method-get-bone-global-pose) for that method, it says:

> Returns the overall transform of the specified bone, with respect to the skeleton. Being relative to the skeleton frame, this is not the actual "global" transform of the bone.

So it would seem that you're not getting the global transform in the context of the scene tree, but rather the global transform in the context of the skeleton. So this is likely more appropriate:

```gd
if not physical_bone_simulator_3d.is_simulating_physics():
    bone.global_transform = skeleton_3d.global_transform * skeleton_3d.get_bone_global_pose(0)
```

There is however also a note saying:

> **Note:** This is the global pose you set to the skeleton in the process, the final global pose can get overridden by modifiers in the deferred process, if you want to access the final global pose, use [SkeletonModifier3D.modification_processed](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_skeletonmodifier3d.html#class-skeletonmodifier3d-signal-modification-processed).

So I'm guessing you'll ideally want to do this transform update in such a signal handler instead of `_physics_process`.

Doing so also seems to fix the issue of the bone shape's debug rendering looking like it's actually following the player when it isn't.

> while it can be detected by Raycast3D just fine

This seems to be because your `RayCast3D` has its mask set up to hit layer 1, whereas your `Area3D` is set up to detect overlaps with layer 2.
Thank you very much. That fixed the issue. Turns out the problem is I didn't realized that skeleton_3d.get_bone_global_pose() doesn't return game world global transform, which cause the issue.
I'll go ahead and close the issue as resolved then.
